response.passage: Welcome to our FAQ on how goods reach your home. Many students ask, do wholesale markets actually manufacture the products they sell? No, wholesale markets act as large storage hubs where traders buy goods in bulk from factories and sell them to smaller shopkeepers. Another common question is whether weekly markets are only for low-income families. In reality, weekly markets are popular because they offer a wide variety of goods at affordable prices for everyone, regardless of their income level. People also wonder if items in malls are always superior to those in local shops. While malls provide a comfortable shopping experience, the quality of basic goods like vegetables or pulses is often identical to what you find in your neighborhood market. Finally, why do prices change as products move through the chain? As goods travel from the producer to the wholesaler, and then to the retailer, each person adds their own costs for transport, storage, and profit, which is why the final price increases by the time it reaches your hands.
response.summary: This passage explains that wholesale markets are distribution hubs rather than factories. It clarifies that weekly markets and local shops serve all people, and explains why prices rise along the supply chain.
